info.title: AI-SRO
info.summary: Workflow Builder: demonstrations in, reviewable skills out.

get.description: Liveness: the process answers. Deliberately touches no dependency.

schema.title: Response List Connections V1 Connections Get

post.description: Open a browser at the system. The operator signs in there, not here.

get.description:
Whether each stored session still works, asked of the systems themselves.

Live rather than remembered: a session that expired an hour ago still looks
connected in the database, and the operator finds out inside a
demonstration. This is what lets the app say it first.

schema.title: Response Check Sessions V1 Connections Health Get

post.description:
Keep the session the operator just created.

Called when they say they are signed in. The cookies are read out of the
browser and encrypted into the vault; nothing about them is returned here.

put.description:
What the connection signs itself back in with, entered once.

This is the difference between a saved session and a connector: a session
dies on the system's schedule, and something has to be able to make a new
one at 3am without waking anybody.

Encrypted into the vault on arrival. No endpoint returns it, nothing logs
it, no recording contains it, and it is typed into no page but the login
page of the host this connection names.

post.description: Sign in now with what is stored, and keep the session it produces.

Headers the executor must send as this session and cannot derive.

The response names the keys and never the values: an endpoint that echoed a
credential back would put it in every proxy log between here and the caller.

schema.title: Response List Recordings V1 Recordings Get

get.description: Null when the demonstration is over or the provider has reaped it.
Playback links, minted per request and short-lived.

schema.title: Response Get Media V1 Recordings  Recording Id  Media Get

post.description:
``recorded_from`` is when the microphone started, for audio.

Without it a transcript's offsets cannot be placed against the frames, and
narration attaches to the wrong steps -- which is worse than none.

Two runs to one skill version.

Runs through Temporal rather than in the request: a failed induction keeps a
history worth reading, and a retry starts from the sealed recordings rather
than from a browser session nobody can reproduce. The caller still waits --
induction takes milliseconds -- but the work is not lost if this process is.

One demonstration to a skill.

The two-run diff proves which values vary; this reads a single run instead,
and says so: the calls are evidence, the description and the parameters are
a model's reading of them, and every parameter it proposes is checked
against a literal in the captured payloads before it survives.

schema.title: Response List Skills V1 Skills Get

post.description: Reword what the skill is for. Changes what finds it, never what it does.

What was asked for, and whether anything can honestly perform it.

Deliberately separate from starting a run: an operator confirms a match
before a write goes out, and that confirmation is what an assisted run
records as its authorisation.

get.description: One person teaches; the tenant knows. This is that, counted.

schema.title: Response List Threads V1 Threads Get

post.description:
Say something and get the whole thread back, decision included.

Nothing is performed here. A matched skill is offered; starting it is the
operator's next request, and that is what makes their confirmation the
authorisation an assisted run records.

Perform the skill at L1.

What the stage means here: `shadow` sends every read and withholds every
write, producing the exact request it would have sent. Above shadow the
writes go out, and the request must name the human who authorised that.

Do the same taught task to several things.

N runs, each with its own idempotency keys, audit record and verification —
so one item failing says nothing about the others, and the failure names
which item it was. A safety limit stops the batch rather than the item.

schema.title: Response List Runs V1 Runs Get

CredentialsRequest.title: CredentialsRequest
CredentialsRequest.description:
Entered once, by a human, and never read back out.

There is no matching response model on purpose: an endpoint that returned a
password would put it in every proxy log between here and the caller.

abandon_reason.title: Abandon Reason
abandon_reason.description: Present means abandon; absent means seal.

objective_key.description: Only for a demonstration whose evidence cannot name it, or the second run of a pair. Otherwise the task names itself.

FrameSummary.title: FrameSummary
FrameSummary.description: Enough to render the timeline. The full frame is fetched per frame.

KnowledgeSummaryModel.title: KnowledgeSummaryModel
KnowledgeSummaryModel.description: What this organisation knows, and how it got there.

ResolutionModel.title: ResolutionModel
ResolutionModel.description:
What the system decided a sentence asked for.

`matched` absent with `choices` present means two skills were too close to
separate; `proposal` present means nothing was taught and this is what the
knowledge base says. Neither is a run.
